mainTopic: Being quoted after death and the late-maturing twenty-year-old; then a new chapter on whether rape or seduction, unlike marriage, forbids a woman's relatives.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רבי יוחנן. דוד's prayer to live in two worlds means being quoted in this world after death, because a quoted תלמיד חכם's lips move in the grave, like a pile of grapes that moves at a touch. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's twenty-year-old without two hairs. It resolves a contradiction with a ברייתא by limiting the ברייתא to someone who shows signs of a סריס. Without such signs, we wait until most of his years, and רבא would first have the person's weight adjusted. After the הדרן of האשה רבה, a new chapter begins: rape or seduction does not create the family prohibitions that marriage creates, and רבי יהודה disagrees about a woman one's father raped. The גמרא learns the rule from the Torah's word 'taking' and from רבא's reading of two פסוקים, where only marriage creates שאר. Finally it explains רבי יהודה's source, 'his father's skirt'. The רבנן instead read that פסוק as forbidding the father's יבמה, which adds extra לאוין or applies after the father's death.

steps.title: דוד's prayer means being quoted in this world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining דוד's prayer: he asked that people would say his Torah teachings in his name in this world after he passed away.
steps.simpleTranslation: [דוד asked] that people will say a teaching in my name in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from just before. דוד's request to 'live in two worlds' meant that his teachings would still be quoted in his name after his death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was how one person could live in this world and the next world at the same time. The answer: when a person is quoted here, it is as if part of him is still living here. This explains why רבי יוחנן cared so much about being quoted by name.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah teaching that has been heard and passed on
Literally 'from my mouth', meaning in my name
This world, as opposed to the next world

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ דְּבַר שְׁמוּעָה מִפִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
phrases.english: that they will say a teaching in my name in this world.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ דְּבַר שְׁמוּעָה מִפִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun just before this section about דוד's request to dwell in two worlds.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Living in two worlds at once seems impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means being quoted in this world while resting in the next.

steps.title: A quoted scholar's lips move in the grave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, teaches that when a תלמיד חכם is quoted in this world, his lips move in the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: Any Torah scholar who is quoted in this world, his lips move in the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the previous step. It shows why being quoted counts as 'living' in this world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word דאמר ('as he said') signals that this teaching is the basis for the idea before it. Being quoted gives the scholar a kind of continued life: his lips move as if he were speaking.

keyTerms.meaning: His lips move, as if speaking

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
Any Torah scholar about whom people say
a teaching in his name in this world,
his lips move in the grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the idea that being quoted means living on in this world.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that being quoted in this world is a form of living in it
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי

steps.title: The פסוק behind the idea
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בן זעירא (or שמעון נזירא) brings a פסוק from שיר השירים about wine that 'moves the lips of those who sleep.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בן זעירא said, and some say it was שמעון נזירא: What is the source? 'And your palate is like the best wine, going to my beloved smoothly, moving the lips of those who sleep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a פסוק for the teaching that a quoted scholar's lips move in the grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are דובב שפתי ישנים, 'moving the lips of sleepers.' The 'sleepers' are read as those who have passed away, and their lips move when their words are spoken.

keyTerms.meaning: Sleepers, read here as those who have died

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Ze'eira said,
and some say it was Shimon the Nazirite:
What is the verse?
"And your palate is like the best wine
that goes to my beloved smoothly,
moving the lips of those who sleep."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 7:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק for the teaching in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: Lips of a quoted scholar move in the grave

steps.title: The picture of a pile of grapes
steps.stepSummary: The word דובב is explained with a picture: a pile of grapes moves as soon as a finger touches it. In the same way, a scholar's lips move as soon as he is quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like a pile of grapes: just as a pile of grapes moves right away when a person puts his finger on it, so too Torah scholars: once people say a teaching in their name in this world, their lips move in the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק works by comparing it to a heap of grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny touch makes the whole grape pile move. In the same way, just saying a teaching in a scholar's name is enough to 'move' his lips. This is why רבי יוחנן wanted his name attached to his teachings.
steps.whatToRemember: Quoting a Torah teaching in the name of the one who said it gives him continued life. That is why רבי יוחנן was so upset to be left out.

phrases.english: Like a pile of grapes:
phrases.notes: This picture explains the word דובב ('moving') in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Just as a pile of grapes,
as soon as a person places his finger on it,
it immediately moves;
so too Torah scholars,
once people say a teaching in their name
in this world, their lips move in the grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word דובב in the פסוק through a comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a small act, quoting a scholar by name, makes his lips move in the grave, just as a touch makes a grape heap move.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the nine-year-old and the twenty-year-old
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which groups a nine-year-old boy together with a twenty-year-old who has not developed two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] Both a nine-year-old and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story and goes back to the משנה. It is setting up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts the nine-year-old (and one day) and the twenty-year-old without two hairs in one group for יבום. The next step will test whether they really share the same status.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on; the rest of the quote is left out

phrases.english: Both a nine-year-old, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: 'and a twenty-year-old who has not developed two hairs.' They are grouped together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the halachic discussion of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה treats a nine-year-old and a twenty-year-old without two hairs the same way.

steps.title: A ברייתא treats the twenty-year-old as a סריס
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a twenty-year-old without two hairs is a סריס who can do neither חליצה nor יבום. A woman in the same situation is an איילונית. This seems to contradict the משנה's grouping.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: A twenty-year-old man who has not developed two hairs: they must bring proof that he is twenty, and he is a סריס. He does neither חליצה nor יבום. A twenty-year-old woman who has not developed two hairs: they must bring proof that she is twenty, and she is an איילונית. She does neither חליצה nor יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with the משנה. Here the twenty-year-old without hairs is not like a nine-year-old at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nine-year-old's relations still count for something in יבום. But the ברייתא says the twenty-year-old is a סריס, who is completely left out of both יבום and חליצה. So how could the משנה put them in the same group?

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction between two sources
Two hairs, the sign of physical maturity
A man who is physically unable to have children
A woman who never physically matures and cannot have children

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is not about the age itself. It is about the status: the משנה seems to treat the twenty-year-old like a nine-year-old, while the ברייתא removes him from יבום and חליצה completely.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
A man twenty years old
who has not developed two hairs:
they must bring proof that he is twenty,
and he is the eunuch,
he neither performs ḥalitza nor levirate marriage.
A woman twenty years old
who has not developed two hairs:
they must bring proof that she is twenty,
and she is the aylonit,
she neither performs ḥalitza nor enters levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 5 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's grouping of a nine-year-old with a twenty-year-old who has not developed two hairs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the twenty-year-old a סריס, excluded from both חליצה and יבום. A nine-year-old's relations still count for something, so the two cannot share one status.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's next task: explaining how the משנה and the ברייתא can both be correct.

steps.title: The ברייתא is only talking about someone who shows signs of a סריס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction. רב said the ברייתא's ruling applies only when the person also developed signs of a סריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it already said about this ברייתא, in the name of רב, that it only applies when he developed signs of a סריס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 6. It says the ברייתא and the משנה are talking about two different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about a twenty-year-old who simply hasn't grown two hairs yet, so he still counts like a child. The ברייתא is about someone who also has the body signs of a סריס, so he is treated as a סריס. Once we see they are different cases, the contradiction goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it already said about this? (introduces an earlier teaching that solves the problem)
Body signs showing that someone is a סריס
A man who cannot have children

phrases.english: Wasn't it stated about it
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא from the last step, the one that seemed to contradict the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said that Rav said
And this is only where he developed signs of a eunuch

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about different people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be about the same twenty-year-old without two hairs, so they seemed to rule differently.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about someone with signs of a סריס. The משנה is about someone who has simply not matured yet.

steps.title: רבא shows the ברייתא's own wording supports this answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the ברייתא says "he is the סריס". That shows it means a clear סריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wording is exact too, because it says "and he is the סריס." Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up רב's answer. He points to a precise word in the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא doesn't just say he is treated like a סריס. It says "he is THE סריס", meaning a real, recognizable one. That fits רב's point that the ברייתא is about someone who shows the signs of a סריס.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also exact (the wording itself supports this)
Learn from it (the point is proven)

phrases.english: Rava said: It is also precise
for it teaches: And he is the eunuch
phrases.notes: The word "the" matters here. It points to someone who is clearly a סריס, not just someone who is late to mature.

phrases.english: Learn from it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 7 from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that the ברייתא is about someone with signs of a סריס.
steps.whatToRemember: At twenty, a man without two hairs is treated as a סריס only if he also has signs of a סריס. Otherwise he is still a late bloomer, as the משנה says, until the age discussed in the next steps.

steps.title: How long do we wait if there are no signs of a סריס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if he shows no signs of a סריס, until what age do we keep treating him as a child?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he never developed signs of a סריס, until how long?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the ברייתא needs signs of a סריס, the גמרא asks about the other case. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without signs of a סריס, he is not called a סריס at twenty. But we can't wait forever. So the גמרא asks at what age we finally decide.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לֹא נוֹלְדוּ לוֹ סִימָנֵי סָרִיס
phrases.english: And when he did not develop signs of a eunuch
until how long?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לֹא נוֹלְדוּ לוֹ סִימָנֵי סָרִיס, עַד כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 7 and asks about the case with no signs of a סריס.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age at which someone with no signs of maturity and no signs of a סריס is finally treated as a סריס.

steps.title: We wait until most of his years
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי חייא taught that we wait until most of his years have passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי חייא taught: until most of his years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a teaching from the school of רבי חייא. We wait until most of a normal lifetime has gone by.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal lifetime is seventy years, so "most of his years" means past the halfway point, about thirty-five. Until then he keeps the status of a child.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי חייא taught
Most of his years (past half of a seventy-year life)

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Chiya taught
until most of his years
phrases.notes: A normal life is seventy years, so this means past the halfway mark, about age thirty-five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We wait until most of his years, about thirty-five.

steps.title: רבא had people change the boy's weight before deciding
steps.stepSummary: When such cases came to רבא, he told them to fatten up a thin boy or slim down a fat one, because the hairs can fall out from either.
steps.simpleTranslation: When people came to רבא, if the boy was thin he told them to fatten him up, and if he was fat he told them to slim him down. These hairs sometimes fall out because of thinness and sometimes because of fatness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how רבא handled these cases in real life. Before deciding someone was a סריס, he had them change the person's weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Missing hairs might not mean he never matured. They may have fallen out because his body was too thin or too fat. So רבא first fixed the weight problem to see if the signs of maturity would show up.

phrases.english: When they came before Rava
if he was thin, he said to them
Go fatten him up
And if he was fat, he said to them
Go make him thin
For these signs
sometimes fall off because of thinness
and sometimes fall off because of fatness

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical step to use before deciding someone is a סריס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before treating someone as a סריס, adjust his body weight, since the signs of maturity may have fallen out from thinness or fatness.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that missing hairs alone do not settle a person's status. We first check whether something else is hiding the signs.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק האשה רבה
steps.stepSummary: The chapter האשה רבה ends here.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, האשה רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line for the chapter. It marks the end of פרק האשה רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a traditional farewell to the chapter, a promise to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a chapter)
The name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaIsha Rabba

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last discussion.

steps.title: New chapter: one may marry relatives of a woman he raped or seduced
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a man may marry the relatives of a woman he raped or seduced, and may marry a woman his father or son raped or seduced. But a man who rapes or seduces a relative of his wife is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may marry relatives of a woman one raped or seduced. One who rapes or seduces a relative of his wife is liable. A man may marry a woman his father raped or seduced, and a woman his son raped or seduced.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It says that rape or seduction does not create the family prohibitions that marriage creates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marrying a woman makes her mother, daughter and so on forbidden to the husband. The משנה teaches that a non-marital act does not do this, so her relatives stay permitted. In the reverse case, a man who sleeps with his wife's relative is liable, because the marriage did create that prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman one is married to (here: one's wife)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'marrying עַל someone' does not mean marrying her too. It means marrying her relative, someone who would be forbidden if she were his wife.

phrases.english: We may marry [relatives] on top of a raped woman
phrases.notes: The words 'on top of' mean marrying her relatives, like her mother or daughter, after being with her.

phrases.english: and on top of a seduced woman;
one who rapes or seduces [a relative] on top of his wife is liable.

phrases.aramaic: נוֹשֵׂא אָדָם אֲנוּסַת אָבִיו וּמְפוּתַּת אָבִיו,
phrases.english: A man may marry a woman his father raped or his father seduced,
a woman his son raped or his son seduced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter right after the הדרן of האשה רבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rape or seduction does not create the marriage-based family prohibitions. Marriage does.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids a woman his father raped or seduced
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees in one case. He forbids a man to marry a woman his father raped or seduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה forbids a woman his father raped and a woman his father seduced.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יהודה, who disagrees with the first opinion about the father's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion permitted a woman one's father had been with outside of marriage. רבי יהודה forbids her. He does not argue about the son's case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda forbids
a woman his father raped and a woman his father seduced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion on part of the ruling in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a woman one's father raped or seduced is forbidden to the son.

steps.title: The משנה matches a ברייתא: raping a woman permits her daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה teaches the same rule as a ברייתא. Raping a woman leaves her daughter permitted, but marrying a woman makes her daughter forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה already teaches what the רבנן taught: if a man raped a woman, he may marry her daughter. If he married a woman, he may not marry her daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by showing that our משנה says the same thing as a known ברייתא. This sets up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the משנה's idea very clear with a direct contrast. Rape does not forbid the daughter, but marriage does. So the prohibition depends on marriage, not on the physical act.

phrases.english: GEMARA: We have learned [in our משנה] that which the Rabbis taught:
If he raped a woman, he is permitted to marry her daughter;
if he married a woman, he is forbidden to marry her daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the משנה to a matching ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rape does not forbid the woman's daughter. Marriage does.

steps.title: Contradiction: a man rumored to be with a woman is forbidden to her relatives
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא says that a man rumored to have been with a woman is forbidden to her mother, daughter and sister. That seems to say a non-marital relationship does forbid her relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it with another source: one who is rumored to have been with a woman is forbidden to her mother, her daughter and her sister!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 15 with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a mere rumor of a relationship forbids her relatives, then an actual rape should surely forbid them. This clashes with the ברייתא that permits the daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: And they contrasted it: one who is rumored [to have been] with a woman
is forbidden to her mother, her daughter and her sister!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a non-marital relationship leaves the woman's relatives permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא forbids the relatives of a woman a man is only rumored to have been with.

steps.title: Answer: that prohibition is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition on the relatives of the rumored woman is only מדרבנן. מדאורייתא they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is forbidden only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in one word: that ברייתא is speaking about a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources can be true. By Torah law, a non-marital act does not forbid her relatives. The חכמים added a protective prohibition of their own, and that is what the second ברייתא teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not by Torah law

phrases.english: It is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing levels of law (Torah law versus rabbinic law)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be talking about the same level of prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law the relatives are permitted. The rabbis forbade them.

steps.title: Challenge: then why does the משנה allow marrying from the start?
steps.stepSummary: If a rabbinic prohibition exists, how can the משנה say 'we may marry' as if it were allowed from the start?
steps.simpleTranslation: And wherever there is a rabbinic prohibition, would the משנה teach 'we may marry' from the start?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 17. It points to the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word נושאין, 'we may marry', which means it is fine to do so לכתחילה. If the rabbis forbade it, the משנה should not have said this. At most it could have said he is not punished after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; allowed to do even before the fact

phrases.english: And wherever there is a rabbinic prohibition,
would it teach 'we may marry' from the start?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא אִיסּוּרָא מִדְּרַבָּנַן תָּנֵי נוֹשְׂאִין לְכַתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17 using the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a rabbinic prohibition applies to the woman's relatives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word נושאין means it is allowed לכתחילה, which does not fit a rabbinic prohibition.

steps.title: Answer: the משנה speaks of marrying after the woman died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means he may marry her relative after the woman he raped or seduced has died. In that case even the rabbinic prohibition does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we learned the משנה, it was about after her death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case of the משנה to after the woman's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbinic prohibition applies while the woman is alive. Once she has died, there is no prohibition at all, so the משנה can say 'we may marry' לכתחילה.

phrases.english: When we learned our משנה,
[it was speaking of] after death.
phrases.notes: He means after the death of the woman who was raped or seduced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to permit marrying her relative even while she is alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of after her death, when no prohibition applies, so marrying is allowed לכתחילה.
steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law, rape or seduction does not forbid the woman's relatives. The rabbis forbade them while she lives, so the משנה's 'we may marry' is about after her death.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source showing that only marriage, not rape or seduction, creates these prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא has dealt with contradictions. Now it asks where in the Torah we see that the prohibitions depend on marriage.

phrases.english: From where are these matters [derived]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the contradictions to asking for the Torah source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that only marriage creates the prohibitions on the woman's relatives.

steps.title: Source: the Torah says 'taking', not 'lying'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that for other forbidden relations the Torah uses the word 'lying' (שכיבה). For the wife's relatives it uses 'taking' (קיחה), which means marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: in all the other cases 'lying' is said, but here 'taking' is said. This tells you that the Torah forbade these relatives only through taking, meaning marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that reads the Torah's choice of words closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah usually describes forbidden relations as 'lying'. For a wife's relatives it says 'taking', which is the language of marriage. So these relatives become forbidden only when the man has married the woman, not through rape or seduction.

keyTerms.meaning: Through the way of taking, meaning marriage

steps.whyThisMatters: This source is the basis for the whole chapter's rule: the prohibitions on a wife's relatives are created by marriage, not by a physical act.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
With all of them 'lying' is stated,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the other forbidden relations listed in the Torah.

phrases.english: but here 'taking' is stated, to tell you:
the Torah forbade [these] through taking.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוּלָּן נֶאֱמַר שְׁכִיבָה וְכָאן נֶאֱמַר קִיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah uses the word 'taking' (marriage) for a wife's relatives, so only marriage creates the prohibition.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: does 'taking' a sister also mean only marriage?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges the idea that 'taking' means only marriage. The Torah also says 'take' about one's sister, yet she is surely forbidden even without marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If so, look at the sister. The פסוק says, 'A man who will take his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter.' Will you also say that only marrying her is forbidden, and lying with her without marriage is allowed?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the proof from step 21. He points to a פסוק where 'take' cannot mean only marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said that 'taking' means marriage, so rape or seduction does not create the prohibition. But the Torah also uses 'take' for one's sister. If 'take' always meant marriage, relations with a sister outside of marriage would be allowed, and that is absurd.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (a phrase that pushes an idea to an absurd result)
By way of, in the manner of

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
If so, regarding his sister, where it is written:
"A man who will take his sister,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:17

phrases.english: his father's daughter or his mother's daughter",

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי דֶּרֶךְ קִיחָה הוּא דַּאֲסִיר,
phrases.english: would you also say that only by way of taking (marriage) is it forbidden,
but by way of lying (without marriage) it is permitted?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's reading of קיחה as marriage from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the word קיחה in the Torah means only marriage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the same word appears for a sister. Reading it as marriage-only would allow relations with a sister outside marriage, which is clearly false.

steps.title: אביי answers: 'taking' means whatever fits the case
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the Torah's word 'taking' has no fixed meaning. Where marriage is possible, it means marriage. Where marriage is impossible, as with a sister, it means lying.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The word 'taking' is written in the Torah without saying what kind. Where the woman is fit to be taken in marriage, it means marriage. Where she is fit only for lying, it means lying.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the ברייתא. The word 'taking' changes its meaning depending on the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man cannot actually marry his sister, because such a marriage would not take effect. So for her, 'take' can only mean lying with her. A wife's relatives, though, are women a man could marry, so there 'take' keeps its normal meaning of marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Takings', the word 'taking' as used in the Torah
One who is fit for, one for whom it is possible

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the sister is allowed in any way. He is saying that 'take' cannot mean marriage for her, because a marriage with her does not work. So the word must mean lying, and she is fully forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִיקּוּחִין כְּתִיבִי בַּתּוֹרָה סְתָם.
phrases.english: He said to him: 'Takings' are written in the Torah without specification.
For one fit for taking (marriage), it means taking;
for one fit only for lying, it means lying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִיקּוּחִין כְּתִיבִי בַּתּוֹרָה סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Taking' always means marriage, so the sister would be forbidden only through marriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Taking' means marriage only where marriage can take effect. For a sister, where it cannot, it means lying.
steps.whatToRemember: The Torah's word 'taking' means marriage only where a real marriage is possible. Otherwise it means lying. So a wife's relatives are forbidden through marriage, but a sister is forbidden in every way.

steps.title: רבא's own proof begins: 'your' granddaughter is forbidden, 'hers' is not
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different source for the rule that a man may marry the daughter of a woman he raped. He starts with a פסוק that forbids a man's own granddaughter, and learns from it that the woman's granddaughter from someone else is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The rule that a man who raped a woman may marry her daughter comes from here. It is written, 'The nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter you shall not uncover.' This implies that her own son's daughter and her own daughter's daughter (not from him) may be uncovered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new path to the same rule. This step sets up the first half of his proof, and the next step brings the second פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses 'your' granddaughter, meaning the man's own descendant. So the woman's granddaughter who is not his descendant is not included, and that implies she is permitted. A contradicting פסוק comes next.

phrases.english: Rava said: If one raped a woman,
that he is permitted to marry her daughter comes from here:
It is written: "The nakedness of your son's daughter
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:10

phrases.english: or your daughter's daughter you shall not uncover";
this implies that the daughter of her own son,
and the daughter of her own daughter, you may uncover.
phrases.notes: 'Her own' means the woman's grandchildren from another man, not from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אָנַס אִשָּׁה מוּתָּר לִישָּׂא בִּתָּהּ מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20's question with a different source from the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who raped a woman may marry her daughter. רבא learns this from the stress on 'your' granddaughter in ויקרא 18:10, which implies that 'her' granddaughter is permitted.

steps.title: רבא settles two פסוקים: one is about rape, one is about marriage
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק forbids the woman's granddaughters, which seems to contradict the first. רבא resolves it: the first פסוק is about a woman he raped, and the second is about his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also written: 'The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover. Her son's daughter and her daughter's daughter you shall not take.' How do these fit together? The first is about rape, and this one is about marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second פסוק that seems to clash with the first one. He shows they are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק implied that the woman's granddaughters are permitted. The second says they are forbidden. The only way both can be true is if they speak about different situations. With a woman he raped, her relatives stay permitted. With his wife, her relatives become forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How do these fit together?

phrases.english: And it is written: "The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:17

phrases.aramaic: אֶת בַּת בְּנָהּ וְאֶת בַּת בִּתָּהּ לֹא תִקַּח״,
phrases.english: her son's daughter and her daughter's daughter you shall not take".
How so?
Here it is about rape; here it is about marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? כָּאן בָּאוֹנָסִין, כָּאן בְּנִשּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's proof by setting the second פסוק against the inference from step 24 and resolving the clash.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting two contradicting פסוקים into two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to contradict each other: one implies that the woman's granddaughters are permitted, and the other forbids them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitting פסוק is about a woman he raped. The forbidding פסוק is about his wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a second, independent Torah source for the rule from the משנה: rape or seduction does not create the family prohibitions that marriage creates.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: one פסוק implies that the woman's granddaughters are allowed, and another forbids them. The answer is that the first is about a woman he raped and the second is about his wife.

steps.title: Why not flip the two verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't reverse רבא's reading of the two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not reverse it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer from the last step by asking why we don't switch which פסוק goes with which case. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the first פסוק (which allows the woman's granddaughter) is about a raped woman, and the second (which forbids her) is about a wife. The challenge asks: why not say the lenient פסוק is about the wife and the strict one is about the raped woman?

keyTerms.meaning: I will reverse it; why not flip the cases?

phrases.english: Let me reverse it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רבא matched each פסוק to its case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's assignment of the strict פסוק to a wife and the lenient one to a raped woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the text seems to force this order, so the opposite order should work just as well.

steps.title: Marriage creates family closeness; rape does not
steps.stepSummary: The forbidden-relations פסוקים speak of שאר (kin). Marriage creates that bond and rape does not, so the strict פסוק must be about a wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The forbidden relations have the word 'kin' written about them. With marriage there is kinship; with rape there is no kinship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the order cannot be flipped. The strict פסוק calls the relatives 'kin', and only a marriage makes a woman's relatives into a man's kin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שאר shows the ban comes from a family bond. Marriage makes the wife's family into his family, but rape creates no such bond. So the strict פסוק fits a wife, and the lenient one fits a raped woman.
steps.whatToRemember: Marriage creates family ties that bring the ערוה bans with them. Rape does not create those ties, so the raped woman's relatives stay permitted.

phrases.english: With forbidden relations, 'kin' is written about them.
phrases.notes: The strict פסוק, ויקרא 18:17, says of her granddaughters 'שַׁאֲרָה הֵנָּה', 'they are her kin'.

phrases.english: With marriage there is kinship,
with rape there is no kinship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to flip the פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: a key word in the פסוק fixes which case it describes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים could be matched to wife and rape in either order.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word שאר means a real family bond, which only marriage creates, so the strict פסוק is about a wife.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source for banning his father's raped woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's view of רבי יהודה, and רב explains his source: 'he may not uncover his father's skirt', meaning a woman his father has 'seen'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה forbids a woman raped by his father, etc. רב גידל said in the name of רב: What is רבי יהודה's reason? The פסוק says 'A man may not take his father's wife, and may not uncover his father's skirt.' A skirt that his father has seen, he may not uncover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, רבי יהודה's ban on marrying a woman one's father raped. רב shows that רבי יהודה learns it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His father's skirt' is read as any woman his father has been with, even without marriage. That is why רבי יהודה forbids her to the son even though his father never married her.

keyTerms.meaning: His father's skirt (a polite way of speaking about relations)

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new מחלוקת: whether relations alone, without marriage, can create a ban for the son.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר בַּאֲנוּסַת אָבִיו וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda forbids a woman raped by his father, etc.
Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו
phrases.english: As it is written: 'A man may not take his father's wife,'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:1

phrases.english: 'and may not uncover his father's skirt.'
A skirt that his father has seen, he may not uncover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה learns from 'his father's skirt' that a woman his father had relations with, even by rape, is forbidden to the son.

steps.title: How do we know the verse is about rape?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know this פסוק is about a raped woman and not just the father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that it is written about a raped woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof that 'his father's skirt' is about a woman his father raped. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק already talks about the father's wife. So we need a reason to read the second half as being about a different case, rape.

phrases.english: And from where do we know it is written about a raped woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for support for רב's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that 'his father's skirt' is about rape and not marriage.

steps.title: The verse comes right after the rape section
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק right before it in the Torah is about a rapist paying fifty silver pieces, so 'his father's skirt' is read in that setting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because just above this פסוק it says: 'And the man who lay with her shall give the young woman's father fifty silver pieces.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק before it deals with rape. So 'his father's skirt' is read as continuing that topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the order of the פסוקים: a law placed next to the rape section is taken to be about rape too. That is how רבי יהודה applies the ban to a woman his father raped.

keyTerms.meaning: Fifty silver pieces, the rapist's fine

phrases.english: Because it is written just above the פסוק:
'And the man who lay with her shall give'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:29

phrases.english: 'to the young woman's father fifty silver pieces.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rape law comes right before the פסוק, so the פסוק is read as being about rape.

steps.title: The רבנן: the verses are not really next to each other
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the proof would work only if 'his father's skirt' came right after the rape law. But another phrase comes between them, so the פסוק is free to teach רב ענן's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? If it were placed right next to it, it would be as you said. Now that it is not placed next to it, it is needed for רב ענן's teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן, who argue with רבי יהודה, reject this proof. They then point to a different use for the פסוק, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between the rape law and 'his father's skirt' stands 'A man may not take his father's wife'. That break means the two are not really side by side, so the proof from their order falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who argue with רבי יהודה

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן: אִי הֲוָה סְמִיךְ לֵיהּ — כִּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ.
phrases.english: And the Rabbis? If it were placed right next to it, it would be as you said.
Now that it is not placed next to it,
phrases.notes: 'A man may not take his father's wife' comes in between the two.

phrases.english: it is needed for the teaching of Rav Anan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's proof from the order of the פסוקים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the order of the פסוקים, not the meaning of the words.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוקים are not truly next to each other, because another phrase separates them.

steps.title: רב ענן: the verse is about the father's יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן in the name of שמואל explains that the פסוק is about a widow waiting for יבום with the man's father, meaning a woman who is 'fit' for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב ענן said in the name of שמואל: The פסוק speaks of a widow waiting for יבום with his father. And what is 'his father's skirt'? A skirt that is fit for his father, he may not uncover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the teaching of רב ענן that the רבנן use this פסוק for. It is about the widow of his father's brother, who is waiting for his father to do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה read 'his father's skirt' as a woman his father has seen. רב ענן reads it as a woman who is set aside for his father. So the פסוק teaches a ban on the father's יבמה, not on a woman the father raped.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do yibum
Fit for, or set aside for, his father

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: 'his father's skirt' means a woman his father has seen, even by rape, so she is forbidden. רבנן: it means his father's יבמה, a woman fit for his father, so a woman his father raped is permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides read the same words, 'his father's skirt'. רבי יהודה says 'that his father saw', and רב ענן says 'that is fit for his father'.

phrases.english: As Rav Anan said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם שֶׁל אָבִיו הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.
phrases.english: The verse is speaking of a widow waiting for yibum with his father.
phrases.notes: She was married to his father's brother, who died childless, so his father is the one meant to do יבום.

phrases.english: And what does 'his father's skirt' mean?
A skirt that is fit for his father, he may not uncover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other teaching that the רבנן say the פסוק is needed for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'His father's skirt' forbids a man to be with the widow who is waiting for yibum with his father.

steps.title: She is already forbidden as his aunt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ענן: why do we need a פסוק to forbid her, when she is already forbidden as his aunt?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you could already get this from the fact that she is his aunt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ענן's reading. The woman waiting for יבום with his father was married to his father's brother, so she is his aunt and already forbidden to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife of one's father's brother is a דודה, and she is already forbidden by her own לאו. So why does the תורה need 'his father's skirt' to forbid her? The question is that the new פסוק seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it from, meaning 'you already have this from another source'
His aunt, here the wife of his father's brother

phrases.english: But let him derive it because she is his aunt!
phrases.notes: She was married to his father's brother, his uncle. That makes her his aunt, who is forbidden in ויקרא 18:14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ענן's reading of the פסוק from step 32 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ענן's claim that 'his father's skirt' forbids the father's יבמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She is already forbidden as a דודה, so a new פסוק for this seems pointless.

steps.title: The פסוק adds a second לאו
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed so that he breaks two לאוין with her instead of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is so that he transgresses two prohibitions with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is not needed to make her forbidden. It is needed to add a second לאו on top of the aunt prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two לאוין can apply to the same act. The aunt לאו already forbids her, and 'his father's skirt' adds one more. So the פסוק is not wasted, because it makes the sin heavier.

keyTerms.meaning: To transgress with her (on her account)

phrases.english: So that he transgresses with her two prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a prohibition: the פסוק adds an extra לאו instead of creating the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is useless because she is already his aunt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק adds a second לאו on top of the aunt prohibition.

steps.title: She already has two לאוין without the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: she is already forbidden as a יבמה לשוק, so she already has two לאוין without the new פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you could already get a second prohibition from the fact that she is a יבמה who may not marry an outsider!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. A widow waiting for יבום may not be with anyone except the יבם, so a second לאו already exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of יבמה לשוק forbids the waiting widow to anyone except the יבם, and the son is not the יבם. So he already breaks two לאוין: aunt and יבמה לשוק. That means 'two לאוין' cannot be the reason for the new פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for יבום, who is forbidden to any man other than the יבם (literally, 'a יבמה to the street')

phrases.english: But let him derive it because of a יבמה to an outsider!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the פסוק adds a second לאו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second לאו already exists through יבמה לשוק, so the new פסוק still adds nothing new.

steps.title: The פסוק adds a third לאו
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed so that he breaks three לאוין with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is so that he transgresses three prohibitions with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer one level higher. The פסוק adds a third לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three לאוין are aunt, יבמה לשוק, and his father's יבמה ('his father's skirt'). The new פסוק still adds something, because it makes three לאוין instead of two.

phrases.english: So that he transgresses with her three prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 35 by raising the count from two to three.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a prohibition: the פסוק adds a third לאו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She already has two לאוין, so the פסוק adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק makes it three לאוין.

steps.title: The פסוק is talking about after the father dies
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the פסוק is about after the father's death. At that point she is no longer a יבמה לשוק, so the פסוק is truly needed for a second לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: it is talking about after his father's death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question of step 35. The פסוק is about after the father has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father, her only יבם, has died, she is no longer waiting for יבום. So the יבמה לשוק prohibition is gone. Still, she was once fit for his father, so 'his father's skirt' forbids her, and together with the aunt לאו that makes two.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'his father's skirt' is not wasted. Either it adds an extra לאו (two, or even three), or it applies after the father's death, when only the aunt prohibition and this פסוק remain.
steps.confusionAlert: Whose death? The father's, the one who was supposed to do יבום. Not her first husband, who has already died.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
After death.
phrases.notes: He means after the father dies. Then she is no longer waiting for יבום, so the יבמה לשוק prohibition no longer applies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 35, instead of the 'three לאוין' answer of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing: the פסוק is placed in a time when the יבמה לשוק prohibition no longer exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She is always a יבמה לשוק, so the פסוק adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the father's death the יבמה לשוק prohibition is gone, so the פסוק supplies a real second לאו.
